transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
Lately I just can’t think straight or make decisions at work the way I used to. It's really frustrating because I’ve always been able to handle my job, but now my mind just feels completely stuck.
Have there been any major changes or stressful events in your life recently, either at work or at home, around the time these difficulties started?

Well, over the past year, I was shortlisted for a regional director role, which brought a lot of pressure to cut costs and deal with a wave of supervisor turnover. I've been working much longer hours at the distribution center and traveling a lot more. All of that extra stress really seemed to kick off these unpredictable ups and downs in my energy.
During those times when your energy is high, do you experience periods where you feel unusually excited, need much less sleep than usual, or feel like your thoughts are racing?

Yes, absolutely. My mind races so fast that I jump from one idea to another and can't even finish a single thought, like I'm running on some extra battery. I'll stay up until two in the morning working on my motorcycle without feeling tired at all, just feeling really wired and snappy.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting two weeks or more where you felt the opposite—unusually down, exhausted, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yes, I've had those low periods off and on for a couple of years, and this current slump has been dragging on since last fall. I've completely lost interest in working on my bike or going fishing with my church friends, and I just end up sitting on the couch. Physically, I feel so exhausted and slowed down that I just shuffle around the house or find myself standing frozen at work.
How long do these periods of high energy, where you feel wired and need less sleep, typically last? Do they go on for several days in a row, or just a few hours?

They definitely last much longer than just a few hours. Usually, those "on" periods go on for days or even a couple of weeks at a time. During those weeks, I feel like I'm running on that extra battery day after day without slowing down.
During those high-energy times, did you ever make impulsive decisions or do things that caused serious problems at work, with your family, or financially?

Yes, during those high times I do some pretty reckless things I’d normally never do. I've put huge charges on our credit card for motorcycle tools and parts without even talking to my wife first. I’ll also find myself driving way too fast on the highway at night, telling myself I’ve got everything under control when I know it's really dangerous.
During this current low period, have you heard or seen things that others couldn't, or had strong beliefs or fears that others told you weren't real?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I don't hear or see things that aren't really there, and I haven't had any strange beliefs or fears of that nature.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a current severe depressive episode characterized by anhedonia, severe fatigue, psychomotor retardation, and significant cognitive difficulties (indecisiveness and inability to think straight at work) lasting since last fall. The patient also has a distinct history of manic episodes characterized by elevated energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, irritability, and reckless behaviors (impulsive spending and dangerous driving) lasting for weeks at a time. The absence of hallucinations or delusions during the current episode confirms the diagnosis of Bipolar affective disorder, current episode severe depression without psychotic symptoms (F31.4).
